data.cultural_impact: The name Sivaji holds great cultural significance in Hinduism. It is a form of reverence for Lord Shiva, who is considered one of the primary deities in Hinduism. Sivaji was the name of several great rulers in ancient India, notably Shivaji Bhonsle, who founded the Maratha Empire in the seventeenth century. The name is deeply entrenched in Indian history and remains a symbol of power, strength, and divine wisdom.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Lord Shiva is the embodiment of supreme consciousness, transcendence, and the something beyond the material existence. He is regarded as the benevolent deity who bestows blessings and protects his devotees from evil and calamity. The name Sivaji carries the spiritual significance of connecting with Lord Shiva, focusing on inner wisdom, and seeking spiritual growth and enlightenment. It is a reminder that the connection with the divine is an essential aspect of a balanced and meaningful life.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sivaji I (1592–1657 CE) was a Maratha king who ruled the Maratha Confederacy from 1630 to 1680. The name Sivaji carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Sivaji I was a king of the Maratha Empire in the 17th century.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Sivaji remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Maya Sivaji in Hyderabad, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Sivaji, which means "God". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Sivaji means "Lord Shiva's army." It is a name revered in Hindu culture, symbolizing the warrior spirit that is dedicated to protecting and upholding the divine will of Lord Shiva.
